main_text.p: objecta fidei practicæ, & Obedientiæ Deo præstan- dæ ex fide promissorum; parum solicitus de cogni- tione Naturæ Divinæ, & Attributorum illuc per- tinentium, modo observantia mandatorum divino- rum integre exhibeatur. Quasi Christiani parum aut nihil interfit, scire quid Deus sit, modo con- stet, quid velit. Propter hanc quoque Crellius il- lius Discipulus, non parum celebratur in Ethicis su- is. Adeo ut Philosophiæ moralis Professores potius censendi sint, quam fidei Christianæ. Imo, ne hanc quoque in quibusdam, nobis integram & inviolatam tradiderunt, cum aliqua lege Christi vera permiserint, & multo plura eadem lege permissa vetuerint. Quid? quod multo pejus est; duo ista Socinianorum Dogmata de Anima humana omnis sensus expers, post egressum e corpore donec ad Christi Adventum e Somno expergefiat; & totalis Interitus, sive Abolitio Impiorum, post Judicium a Christo peractum, omnem plane virtutem e mundo tollunt & omnimodæ morum licentiæ latam portam aperiunt. Cum enim multo major Pars Homi- num, a malo abstineat, & in officio contineatur, supplicii metu potius quam amore virtutis; quid non audebunt ambitiosi, avari, luxuriosi, omniqué nequitiæ dediti quotiescunque ad fraudibus & dolis, aut aperta vi, cupiditates suas explere datum est, si modo perfuadere sibi possint, nullas omnino restare pœnas post hanc vitam à se subeundas, quot- cunque aut qualiacunque flagitia sua in hac vita fue- rint? Idcirco, ne jactent sese Socinicni de morum præceptis, & honestioris vitæ Regulis. Nam & Epicurus has tradidit; qui etiam libros conscripsit de Sanctitate & Pietate adversus Deos, ut Cicero memorat lib. I. de nat. Deorum; cum tamen satis notum

page.notes: Transcription of a single printed page (p. 9) from the running text. Doubtful readings: "Socinicni" in the line "ne jactent sese Socinicni" is probably a printing or scan error for "Sociniani", but I have left the reading as close to the scan as I can; the scan is blurred in the lower half, so some words in the middle (e.g. "ad fraudibus", "quotiescunque") are uncertain and should be checked against the original. Also "Dogmata", "Somno", "Adventum" are as read. The last line "notum" is the first word of an unfinished sentence at the page foot, a fragment that continues on the next page. Show-through and scan noise were ignored.
